extracted.intended_audience: University students (Duke) interested in comedy writing and improvisation; beginners through those with existing improv skills
extracted.subtask_description: Develop television-style comedy stories by creating writer's-room story outlines and then rehearsing/iterating them through improvisation, culminating in an in-class performance. The course accommodates beginners and experienced improvisers and includes optional prep workshop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a story idea with a writer's table
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a writer's table to develop a story idea for each show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class will develop a story idea with a writer's table — mirroring how Curb Your Enthusiasm originates stories — as the first step in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a story outline (no script)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a story outline for the developed idea; no full script is written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He develops a story outline for each show but no script is written. The outline should capture the story beats that will guide improvisation rather than line-by-line dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvise the outline until it works
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform iterative improvisation of the outlined idea, refining through practice until the piece feels successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show is then improvised by the actors. This class will improv our idea until we think it works — indicating an iterative, performative testing process rather than a single run-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform the finished work
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the finalized improvised piece in performance during the last class meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the last class we will perform our finished work — a summative, public demonstration of the developed outline and rehearsed improvisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible to beginners and experienced improvisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Course is geared to people with no improv skills or established skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The class explicitly welcomes both novices and those with existing improv experience, implying instruction and pacing suitable for a mixed-skill cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional one-day free improv workshop (preparation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-day optional free improv workshop is offered before the class begins as an introduction or refresher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This workshop serves as optional preparatory training for those new to improv or needing a refresher, reducing entry barriers and aligning skill levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcomes: comedy writing skills and new improv form
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunity to work with other writers in developing comedy writing skills and learning a new improv form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course goals include developing comedy writing skills, learning the specific Curb Your Enthusiasm-style improv form (outline-based, unscripted performance), and collaborative practice with peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional modes: hands-on activity, video viewing, writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Course activities include hands-on activity (e.g., computer, art), viewing videos, and writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mix of practical exercises, multimedia examples, and written work will be used to teach the form and support skill development.
